correctness.rationale: For m>=2 every derivation of the unital truncation k1+V+V tensor V fixes 1 and cannot have a scalar generator component: the distinct degree-two terms in D(x_i x_j x_i)=0 exclude it. Thus D is determined uniquely by P:V->V and Q:V->V tensor V, and degree-two action L_P=P tensor I+I tensor P. The equations D^2=D are P^2=P, L_PQ+QP=Q, and L_P^2=L_P; the latter is 2P tensor P=0, forcing the zero map off char2. In char2 decompose V=U+Z for projection P rank r, s=m-r. Q(U) belongs to U tensor U+Z tensor Z and Q(Z) to mixed tensors, yielding dimension r^3+3rs^2, rank D=r+2rs, and the Gaussian finite-field count. **A crucial additional result beyond the prior exact polynomial** is full Aut(A_m)-conjugacy transitivity within each projection rank: M in GL(V) moves any P to diag(I_r,0), and quadratic shear S maps the standard D_P to any admitted Q since L_PS+SP=Q for S=Q in char2. These m+1 orbits are vector bundles over smooth connected GL_m/(GL_r x GL_s) projection strata, dimension 2rs+r^3+3rs^2, hence the reduced component classification. Independent exhaustive two-generator GF2 generator images gave full-rank spectrum {0:1,2:256,3:96} matching r=(0,2,1); source check_orbits enumerates all 1536 automorphisms for this boundary case. Full component proof remains geometric, not finite-computational.

For m>=2 unitalization imposes no further derivations: scalar generator parts already vanish, so those counted formulas ARE prior and should NOT be claimed novel.
